historical_references.reference: Aisha bint Abu Bakr was a prominent wife of the Prophet Muhammad and one of the most beloved figures in Islamic history. She was born in Mecca around 614 AD and married Muhammad in 622 AD, shortly before the Hegira (emigration) to Medina. Aisha was known for her intelligence, beauty, and strength of character, and played an important role in the political and military affairs of the early Islamic community.
historical_references.context: Marriage to Prophet Muhammad and role in early Islamic community

historical_references.reference: Fatima bint Muhammad, also known as Umm Aisha or simply Umm Aisha, was a sister of Ali ibn Abi Talib and a wife of the Prophet Muhammad. She was born around 605 AD and married Muhammad in 622 AD, shortly before the Hegira. Umm Aisha was an accomplished poetess and scholar, and her poetry was highly regarded in early Islamic society. She is also remembered for her role as a leader in the defense of Medina during the Battle of the Trench (627 AD).
historical_references.context: Marriage to Prophet Muhammad and role in defense of Medina during Battle of the Trench
